title: Restriction to replete full quasicategories and comparison on cores
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functor equivalences, coherent natural equivalences, full subcategories, cores and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Work in a universe containing all the displayed simplicial sets. Let $P:C\to D$ be a coherent functor equivalence of small quasicategories, and let $V\subseteq D_0$ be invariant under equivalence edges: if $d\in V$ and $d\simeq d'$ in $D$, then $d'\in V$. Put $U=\{c\in C_0:P(c)\in V\}$. Write $C_U,D_V$ for the full simplicial subsets on those vertices. They are quasicategories, and $P$ restricts to a coherent functor equivalence $C_U\to D_V$. A chosen coherent quasi-inverse of $P$ restricts to a quasi-inverse of this map; the chosen units and counits restrict as well. The induced map of cores $C_U^\simeq\to D_V^\simeq$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. More generally every coherent functor equivalence $F:E\to E'$ between small quasicategories induces a weak homotopy equivalence $E^\simeq\to(E')^\simeq$: the quasi-inverse restricts to cores and the coherent inverse equivalences give simplicial homotopies on the cores. Empty full subcategories are allowed.

source.place: HTT Proposition 3.2.2.14, the full-subcategory mapping test; general restriction and core argument extracted from the returned Step 26. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result; HTT is requested in report.md.

proof.text: For any quasicategory $X$ and set $W$ of vertices, its full simplicial subset $X_W$ is a quasicategory. An inner horn has dimension at least two and contains every vertex of its simplex. Fill a horn in $X_W$ inside $X$; the filler has the same vertices, all in $W$, so fullness puts it in $X_W$. Moreover, an edge of $X_W$ is an equivalence there exactly when it is one in $X$: an ambient inverse and its two inverse triangles use only the two endpoints, so all three simplices lie in the full subset. This proves the quasicategory assertions for $C_U,D_V$, without assuming either vertex set nonempty.

source.place: Section 1.2.11, full subcategories, and Proposition 1.2.5.3 with its following paragraph; explicit inverse-restriction and core-cylinder argument written by the agent. Application: proof of Proposition 3.2.2.14. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose the specified quasi-inverse $Q:D\to C$, unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}_C\simeq QP$ and counit $\varepsilon:PQ\simeq\mathrm{id}_D$, with their inverse edges and inverse triangles in the corresponding functor simplicial sets. A simplicial map preserves equivalence edges: apply it to an inverse edge and the two inverse triangles. Evaluation at an object is such a simplicial map, so every component of $\eta$ and $\varepsilon$ is an equivalence. For $d\in V$, the inverse component of $\varepsilon_d$ connects $d$ to $PQ(d)$; invariance of $V$ gives $PQ(d)\in V$, hence $Q(d)\in U$. Also $P(U)\subseteq V$ by the definition of $U$. Thus fullness restricts the actual maps $P,Q$ to maps $p:C_U\to D_V$ and $q:D_V\to C_U$ in every degree.

source.place: Section 1.2.11, full subcategories, and Proposition 1.2.5.3 with its following paragraph; explicit inverse-restriction and core-cylinder argument written by the agent. Application: proof of Proposition 3.2.2.14. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Restrict the map $C\times\Delta^1\to C$ representing $\eta$ to $C_U\times\Delta^1$. Its vertices are $c$ and $QP(c)$ with $c\in U$. The latter lies in $U$ because $P(c)\in V$ and the preceding argument applies to $d=P(c)$. Fullness therefore makes this a transformation $\mathrm{id}_{C_U}\to qp$. The inverse transformation and the two inverse triangles restrict too: their maps $C_U\times\Delta^2\to C$ have only the same endpoint functors as vertices, and every such value lies in $U$. The identical argument on $D_V$ restricts $\varepsilon$, its inverse and its inverse triangles, since $PQ(V)\subseteq V$. These are the chosen coherent natural equivalences for $p,q$, so $p$ is a coherent functor equivalence with precisely the claimed restricted data.

proof.text: Now let $F:E\to E'$ be any coherent functor equivalence and choose inverse $G$ and the two coherent natural equivalences of the composites with identities. Preservation of inverse-triangle witnesses gives restrictions $f:E^\simeq\to(E')^\simeq$ and $g:(E')^\simeq\to E^\simeq$. Each of the chosen natural equivalences is a map $H:X\times\Delta^1\to X$ for $X=E$ or $E'$, with endpoints the appropriate composite and the identity (either chosen orientation suffices). Its component at every vertex is an equivalence, by evaluation of the inverse-triangle witnesses. The next step checks that $H$ restricts to $X^\simeq\times\Delta^1\to X^\simeq$.

source.place: Section 1.2.11, full subcategories, and Proposition 1.2.5.3 with its following paragraph; explicit inverse-restriction and core-cylinder argument written by the agent. Application: proof of Proposition 3.2.2.14. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Check this restriction on edges. For an equivalence edge $a:x\to y$ in $X$, an edge $(a,t\to t)$ maps under $H$ to an equivalence because the endpoint functor preserves equivalence edges. An edge $(\mathrm{id}_x,0\to1)$ maps to the equivalence component of the transformation. For the remaining mixed edge $(a,0\to1)$, take the product $2$-simplex with vertices $(x,0),(y,0),(y,1)$, whose coordinates are the degeneracy of $a$ repeating $y$ and the string $(0,0,1)$. Its image gives a triangle with the mixed edge as long side and the preceding two types as consecutive sides. In $hX$ the long-side class is their composite by [lem-coef-homotopy-category-triangle-calculus], so is invertible. The same cited statement represents the inverse class by an edge and realizes both inverse equations as $2$-simplices. Thus the mixed edge is an equivalence under the definition using inverse triangles. Every edge of the product has one of these types, and every simplex of the core is characterized by its edges. Hence $H$ has the asserted restriction, in every degree, with all simplicial operators inherited from $H$.

source.place: Section 1.2.11, full subcategories, and Proposition 1.2.5.3 with its following paragraph; explicit inverse-restriction and core-cylinder argument written by the agent. Application: proof of Proposition 3.2.2.14. Read online; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: The two restricted maps of step 4 and the two restricted cylinders of step 5 have endpoints $gf,\mathrm{id}_{E^\simeq}$ and $fg,\mathrm{id}_{(E')^\simeq}$. Apply [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]: it allows either endpoint orientation and imposes neither Kan nor nonemptiness hypotheses. It proves that the specified induced core map $f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Apply this general conclusion also to $p$ of step 3, with inverse $q$, to obtain $C_U^\simeq\to D_V^\simeq$. If $V$ is empty, so is $U$, and all restrictions and cylinders are the unique maps with empty domain; the same cited lemma still applies. All constructions are products, subsets and restrictions in the fixed containing universe.
